text.p: - Russia's economic security, as viewed by Interior Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Kulukov, may contradict economic expediency.
- The Russian government's intention to reduce pensions for retired people who are still working would be a disaster for many Russian pensioners.
- The State Duma lower house of the Russian parliament is trying to curb the independent status of central bank.
- The main controlling board of the President's Administration is playing an increasingly active role in strengthening state power in Russia.

- With an apparent cooling in political and economic relations between Russia and the United States, scientific and technological links seem to be the only working elements in cooperation between the two countries.
- The time of the "easy oil" in the Russian North is over, big investments and expensive new technology are essential to continue effective work there.
- Pensions are the only means of survival for many Russian old people, and delays in paying them bring people close to starvation.

- Complicated relations between the Russian political, financial and business elites determine to a great extent a course of events in the country which seems to be entering a period of political stagnation.
